bullets.title: S&P hits all-time high; Nasdaq futures +1.1% as tech rally extends
bullets.body: The S&P 500 reached a new all-time high intraday while Nasdaq 100 futures climbed as much as 1.1%, with broad indices up Dow +1.49%, S&P +1.28%, Nasdaq +1.85%, Russell 2000 +1.24% at midday. Barclays notes 85% of S&P 500 companies have beaten Q2 earnings estimates vs. a 76% historical average, with EPS up 25.1% YoY led by Big Tech. Citadel's Scott Rubner characterizes July's selloff as a positioning reset, not a bull market ending.

bullets.title: Mega-cap tech overbought after 20%+ week; MSFT, AMZN at new extremes vs. 50-DMA
bullets.body: MSFT and AMZN surged more than 20% in the past week, moving from solidly below their 50-DMAs to well into overbought territory. AMZN separately crossed $3 trillion market cap for the first time, joining NVDA, GOOGL, MSFT, and AAPL in that club—though Bezos filed to sell ~15M shares (~$4.07B) and NJ AG filed an antitrust suit over delivery driver practices, weighing stock -2.5% midday.

bullets.title: Hedgeye Quad shifts from Quad4 → Quad3 (Aug) with Quad1 in sight for Sep; favors Tech, REITs, Energy
bullets.body: Hedgeye's monthly Quad model shifted from Quad4 in July to Quad3 in August, with Quad1 nowcasted for September. The Quad3 environment favors Tech/Software, REITs (XLRE), Energy, and Healthcare; Redbook Retail Sales came in at +8.7% YoY with a +100bps sequential tick. Recent gains remain concentrated in short squeezes, profitless tech, and a handful of mega-caps—creating elevated near-term risk.

bullets.title: US drafts ban on Chinese data center optical components; COHR, LITE, AAOI surge 11-14%+
bullets.body: Reuters reported the Trump administration is drafting a ban on imports of new Chinese optical transceivers used in AI data centers, with an FCC rule expected this year. COHR +14.4% and LITE rallying, with AAOI also sharply higher; Morgan Stanley notes Chinese suppliers Innolight and Eoptolink represent ~50% of the transceiver market but non-Chinese suppliers lack capacity to immediately fill the gap. InP substrate supply from China (AXTI) represents a critical bottleneck for scaling US optical production.

bullets.title: Bessent signals possible Iran-Hormuz deal Tuesday/Wednesday; oil reverses sharply lower
bullets.body: Treasury Secretary Bessent said on CNBC a deal to open the Strait of Hormuz could come Tuesday or Wednesday, sending WTI crude down as much as 4.9% to ~$76.37 from earlier highs near $86+. Qatar confirmed diplomatic language has been drafted but said there is no set agenda for direct US-Iran talks; Iran separately threatened US warships and proposed a temporary control arrangement with Oman. Aramco CEO warned that even if Hormuz reopened today, rebuilding inventories could take 18 months.

bullets.title: Bessent active on FX: backs BoJ yen stabilization, references FIMA repo tool, reassures Europe on reserves
bullets.body: Bessent told CNBC that Japan is making serious efforts to stem yen devaluation and that the Bank of Japan will do what is needed; he explicitly referenced the Fed's FIMA repo facility as functionally equivalent to FX swap lines and indicated it is reasonable to consider upsizing it. He also warned that if the yen weakens, other currencies would follow, and reassured Europeans that recent euro moves were just a reallocation of reserves. BOJ data, however, showed no clear evidence of large-scale intervention on Monday, with USDJPY recovering ~300 pips from intervention lows.

bullets.title: Japan 10Y JGB auction posts 2nd-worst tail in two decades as buyers step away
bullets.body: The Japanese 10-year JGB auction experienced its second-largest tail movement in 20 years as demand collapsed, raising concerns about stability in the global bond market. This coincides with the BOJ hiking rates once this year and Bessent backing further BoJ normalization; the dysfunction in JGBs is a cross-asset risk for US Treasuries given carry trade dynamics and JPM's warning that rapid JPY appreciation triggers VaR-driven liquidations in Asian equities.

bullets.title: JOLTS June openings 7.36M, miss vs 7.4-7.6M consensus; labor market gradually softening
bullets.body: June JOLTS job openings came in at 7.359M, below consensus estimates of 7.4-7.59M across multiple bank surveys, with May revised down to 7.537M. The quits rate held unchanged at 2.0%, well below the 3% peak, signaling workers remain disinclined to job-hop. Morgan Stanley maintains its July payroll forecast at 70K with upside risks from goods-sector openings; wage inflation expected to stabilize around 3.5% into 2027.

bullets.title: ISM Manufacturing 55.6 in July—best since 2022—supports cyclical broadening narrative
bullets.body: US ISM Manufacturing hit 55.6 in July, a roughly four-year high, beating the 54.0 forecast. Goldman Sachs cited this as supporting a cyclical broadening narrative alongside tech strength, with JPMorgan noting the print supports industrials across their coverage.

bullets.title: Macro regime: Hedgeye flags inflation re-accelerating; TLT remains Core Short
bullets.body: Oil is up 20% month-over-month and Hedgeye's inflation nowcast is re-accelerating, making TLT (duration) a recommended Core Short. The bond market is currently pricing no change to the Quad3 shift view, and Bessent's comment that Fed is in a 'detox' period adds complexity to rate cut expectations. BofA's Bull & Bear Indicator is at one of its most extreme sell readings since 2000 (63% historical hit rate).

bullets.title: SPX vol structure anomalous: 0DTE straddle at lows despite 20% realized 5-day vol
bullets.body: The SPX zero-DTE straddle is pricing just $25 or ~33bps—near the lowest levels seen—despite 5-day realized volatility running at 20% with a 1.5% SPX move the prior session. Dealers are reportedly slamming index vol while buying single-stock calls, creating a divergence that has historically resolved violently. VIX itself is up 2.5% to 16.25 even as S&P adds 1.3%.

bullets.title: NVIDIA pivoting Rubin Ultra from 12-Hi to 8-Hi HBM4, shifting AI from scale-up to scale-out
bullets.body: Citi reports NVIDIA is reportedly considering shifting Rubin Ultra from 12-Hi to 8-Hi HBM4, reducing per-GPU memory capacity by 33% (192GB vs 288GB) but expanding NVLink domain to 576 GPUs per system—increasing aggregate HBM capacity by 433% to 110.6TB. This scale-out pivot is driven by persistent HBM supply tightness, as memory suppliers prioritize higher-margin server DDR5, SOCAMM2, and eSSD. Wolfe Research's SKHY initiation (Outperform, $200 PT) argues DRAM/HBM supply constraints persist through CY28, with SKHY primary supplier to NVIDIA for HBM.

bullets.title: Anthropic financing boom: Blackstone opens ~$36B debt package; Google built $200B infrastructure program
bullets.body: Blackstone is opening early talks on a potential second debt financing package for Anthropic of at least $36B to purchase Google TPU chips, following a similar $35B package in June. Separately, Google assembled a ~$200B infrastructure financing program tied to Anthropic with Broadcom backstopping payments; Anthropic also struck a $10B compute deal with Volta in Norway. Morgan Stanley sees AI-driven issuance surging with spreads widening but equity/credit risks described as 'contained.'

bullets.title: Accenture AI implementation share jumps to 58%; only 19% of enterprises have AI at scale
bullets.body: UBS notes Accenture's share of large enterprises (>10K employees) identifying it as the preferred AI implementation partner rose to 58% from 47% in October 2025, while only ~19% of enterprises have AI deployed at scale—implying a multi-year demand runway. AI budgets are increasingly tied to measurable outcomes (labor productivity, cost takeout) rather than pilot programs; Gartner separately raised FY26 EPS guidance to ≥$14 on AI-driven demand and improving retention.

bullets.title: European hedge funds de-grossed sharply in July; IT most net sold, Materials most net bought
bullets.body: European Fundamental L/S managers were up 0.5% in July, outperforming US-focused managers (-2.9%) and Asia-focused managers (-15.2%). Industrials was the most net sold sector; Information Technology was net sold after 4 of the prior 5 months of buying. Materials—particularly Chemicals via short covering—was the most net bought. Semiconductors & Equipment were among the most net sold European industries.

bullets.title: US Army depleted 'virtually all' ATACMS and PrSM missiles in five-month Iran conflict
bullets.body: Reuters reports the US Army has used nearly all of its long-range land-based missiles (ATACMS and PrSM) during the five-month Iran war, raising resupply and production capacity concerns for defense contractors. This is a potential structural tailwind for defense capex but also signals the conflict is more intense and durable than market consensus has priced.

bullets.title: Warsh Fed strategy could weaken dollar; Commerzbank warns of yield-tightening approach
bullets.body: Commerzbank warns that Kevin Warsh's monetary policy approach—allowing markets to tighten financial conditions through higher long-term bond yields rather than Fed rate hikes—could structurally weaken the US dollar. Bessent separately said the Fed is undergoing a 'detox' period, and BofA recommends targeting specific FX pairs (JPY and GBP) rather than broad FX volatility if the Fed resumes hikes.

bullets.title: Cloudflare launches AI agent payment infrastructure; NET hits 52-week high ahead of earnings
bullets.body: Cloudflare announced Cloudflare Wallets and cloudflare.pay to enable AI agents to transact online safely with spending caps and merchant whitelists. NET hit a new 52-week high (+4.6% on the day, +47.8% YTD) with options implying an ~11.3% earnings move; Q2 consensus shows $664.7M revenue beating guidance midpoint with a 19-of-20 revenue beat track record. ANET also hit a 52-week high (+2.6%, +61.3% YTD) ahead of its F2Q26 print.

bullets.title: Memory sold out through 2027: HBM absorbing ~70% of DRAM capacity; CXMT advancing on commodity DRAM
bullets.body: Global DRAM and HBM capacity for 2027 is reported as fully allocated per Digitimes, with HBM potentially absorbing ~70% of total DRAM capacity globally; MU, Samsung, and SanDisk are reportedly fully presold on 2027 NAND. Memory suppliers are seeing only 60-70% order fulfillment vs. requested volumes. Separately, China's CXMT is preparing to produce LPDDR6 in small quantities by year-end, and HP, Asus, and Acer are adopting CXMT chips amid the memory shortage—though advanced HBM/DDR5 is unlikely to face CXMT competition due to export controls on advanced lithography.

bullets.title: AI boom driving one-third of recent US growth; White House hosting AI model-testing review today
bullets.body: JPMorgan estimates the AI boom is responsible for roughly one-third of recent US economic growth, while multiple analysts note GPU availability remains tight with rental prices up 50-60%. The White House is hosting AI companies today to review a new model-testing framework. Morgan Stanley's quant strategy recommends staying invested in momentum as the cycle transitions from early to mid, favoring quality.
